testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10.75 inches.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10.75 inches square.

questions.question: Why should you do routine vehicle inspections?
questions.correctAnswerText: To stay safe.
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle is to protect yourself and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Does air pressure in tires decrease in very hot weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Air expands when it gets hotter, so tire pressure increases in very hot weather. Stop often to check your tires and prevent blowouts or fires.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half your strength.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then brake again.

questions.question: What should you do when transporting cargo?

options.text: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
Don't use your mirrors to look behind your vehicle.
Hold your cell phone in case of an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo and securing devices before you start driving. After you begin, check them within the first 50 miles, then every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after each break.

questions.question: How does fatigue affect driving?

options.text: It has little effect on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can hurt your driving.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous and increases crash risk. Take steps before driving to avoid becoming fatigued.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the governor decides when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person you should worry about while driving?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle.
A child on the side of the road.
A construction worker on the side of the road.
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.
questions.explanation: Watch out for people not paying attention to traffic. Be careful around road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number varies by vehicle.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: How should you press the brake pedal when stopping?

options.text: Press it repeatedly, but don't hold it down continuously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down slowly.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal slowly and gradually.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the passenger compartment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil that builds up in the system. Water and oil can damage the brakes. Use manual drains every day.

questions.question: What is special about driving dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They require special care to drive.
Usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require special care to drive.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity. The load weight can also shift during driving.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Check your vehicle before driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness before a trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: Prevent drowsiness by getting enough sleep before the trip, planning your route and stops ahead of time, driving with a passenger, and driving when you are normally awake.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If these build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during travel.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo can:

options.text: Hurt or kill the driver during a quick stop.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt or kill the driver during a quick stop.
questions.explanation: Unsecured cargo is dangerous. During a sudden stop, loose cargo can fall and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should check your mirrors:
questions.correctAnswerText: More often than usual.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of normal driving. Check them even more often when changing lanes.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle compared to yours:

options.text: Will usually stop faster than your vehicle.
Will usually take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Will take about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will usually stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can usually stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to follow behind other vehicles.

questions.question: When you change lanes:

options.text: Other vehicles will likely get out of your way.
You should change lanes slowly and smoothly.
You should change lanes inside an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should change lanes slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle safe and gives other drivers time to see and react to your movements.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tightened.
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each trip. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it slows down enough, brake gently and pull off the road. Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Apply your brakes as you steer.
Turn more than needed to get extra clearance from the object.
Turn only enough to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only enough to miss the object.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid an object, turn only as much as needed to clear it. Do not apply the brakes while turning.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailers are straight.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start your trip. On a vehicle with a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Crashes from tired drivers happen more often at night than any other time.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, drivers must check that the cargo is secure every:
questions.correctAnswerText: 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
It ensures that the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It holds drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles.
It plans the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets you tell the motor carrier about problems that could affect safe driving or cause a breakdown. You should fill one out after each day of driving if required. Note any issues that affect safety or could lead to mechanical failure.

questions.question: When inspecting a vehicle, you must check all of the following, except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating range.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge during a vehicle inspection, make sure it works. The gauge should show normal pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If equipped, the oil temperature gauge should rise gradually to the normal operating range.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: In an air tank
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve is located in the air tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: Your vehicle's brakes need repair if:

options.text: The brake pads are not covered in grease.
The brake pads are not covered in oil.
The brake pads are worn thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake pads are worn thin.
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are broken or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts you mentally and takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:

options.text: With the front bumper on top of the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area, staying within the boundaries.

questions.question: During inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil or grease.
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes should not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be placed on an incline.
Should be placed on a decline.
Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to be running.
questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to operate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brakes that work with compressed air.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should do all of the following except:

options.text: Make sure the truck is not overloaded.
Make sure the cargo is balanced.
Make sure the cargo is secured properly.
Place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place breakable items under heavier items.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured, balanced, and within weight limits. Breakable items should not be placed under heavier items.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Always pump the brakes several times before holding down the brake pedal.
Press down the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in ABS and non-ABS vehicles. ABS automatically prevents wheel lockup when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, your minimum following distance should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Six seconds.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should check the system.

questions.question: Slippery roads usually:

options.text: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Drive carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Should not be used on any vehicle.
Should not be used on the front of a bus.
Should not be used on trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: While driving, your mirrors:

options.text: Should only be used when changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving to see traffic around you. Mirrors also help you spot problems on your own vehicle.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Leave more space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance to the vehicle in front of you. This reduces sudden stops and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: Which surface is the most slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it is warm enough to melt the ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: What does intrastate driving mean?

options.text: Driving within a single state only
Driving from one state to another

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving within a single state only
questions.explanation: Intrastate means you drive a commercial vehicle only within one state, and your cargo does not begin or end outside that state.

questions.question: How long should it take for oil pressure to reach normal after starting an engine?
questions.correctAnswerText: A few seconds
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to skip a step.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to skip a step.
questions.explanation: Following the same order each time helps you remember all the steps. This reduces the chance of missing something during inspection.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but each has separate hoses and lines.
Both systems use the same lines and hoses.
One system is primary and a second system is a backup if the first fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
